title: Claude Code for non-developers: a small first task
h1: claude code for non-developers: start with one folder
description: Start with a bounded file task, write a brief you can verify, and compare Dusk Bot chat with Claude's terminal-free knowledge-work experience.
keywords: claude code tutorial for non developers
answer: you can start with claude code without making software your first project. in dusk bot, a bot can think with claude through its official command-line app while you text it in plain words. begin with files you intentionally supply and a result you can inspect. if you want anthropic's own terminal-free knowledge-work experience, cowork, now becoming part of claude, is another route.[^1][^2][^3]
og_line: start with a result you can inspect.

sections.h: pick a job that does not need a terminal lesson
sections.md:
choose a small set of files you understand: notes from a personal project, a reading packet or a planning document. the first job should be to inspect and summarize those files, leaving the originals alone. avoid a request to reorganize your whole computer.

the important skill is writing a brief you can check. name the input, what counts as finished, what should remain untouched and what to do when information is missing. the [ai agent introduction](/guides/what-is-an-ai-agent) explains why those limits matter when a program can take several steps instead of just answering a question.

sections.h: set up one bot for that job
sections.md:
in dusk bot, choose **New bot** and give it a name, shape, colour and one job in plain words. choose the ai for the bot. dusk has no model of its own: it runs the vendors' official command-line apps on the machine where the bots live, and you sign in yourself.[^1][^4]

work with the ai you already sign in to, and check your provider's current terms for the use you intend. do not assume installing a different desktop interface changes those terms. dusk bot can also take an api key or a local model, but you do not need to compare every option before trying one bounded task.[^1]

drop files into the chat or use **Attach files**. dusk accepts documents, spreadsheets, pictures and screenshots. the work it makes appears in the chat and lives in the bot's folder, or a project folder you give it. use a copy of your first packet if you are experimenting.[^5]

ask it to identify what it could read before you request a summary. then ask for an outline with a source for each point and a list of unresolved questions. those are instructions to give the bot, not an example of an output it has already produced. check the outline against the files yourself.

replies stream in, and a line shows the tools the bot uses. send another message if you see it heading toward the wrong task. **Cmd .** on mac, or **Ctrl .** on windows and linux, stops it. questions can come as **Allow** or **Deny** cards.[^4]

start a new bot on **Ask for approval** for a few days. that setting covers commands and file changes. connected-app sends have their own sending setting, while other app changes should be kept read-only or carry an explicit ask-first instruction. for the first file exercise, there is no need to connect mail, chat or payments.[^6]

if the summary misses a decision, point to the relevant source and say what was missing. if it uses a tone you dislike, give a precise correction. dusk bots remember what you tell them, and you can read and edit their notes in **Memory**. you can also turn memory off.[^7]

keep task-specific instructions separate from durable preferences. "use short paragraphs" may be useful across work; a deadline in one document may not be. when you have a method worth repeating, read about [skills](/guides/claude-skills) to understand how reusable instructions can help with a repeated method.

sections.h: when another interface is a better fit
sections.md:
anthropic describes cowork as bringing claude code's agentic capabilities to knowledge work without requiring a terminal. it is included in paid plans. anthropic now describes cowork and chat as one claude, with cowork brought in automatically for file work.[^2][^3]

the [cowork pricing guide](/guides/claude-cowork-pricing) helps if you want that route. dusk bot fits a different choice: keeping your own named bots and conversations, with a model per bot. neither approach removes the need to review a result. if you cannot tell whether the answer is correct, choose a smaller first task or ask someone who understands the material to check it.

faq.q: can i use claude code without a terminal?
faq.a: dusk bot lets you text a bot while it runs the official command-line ai app. anthropic also describes cowork as a terminal-free knowledge-work experience. they are different product paths.[^1][^2]

faq.q: do i need to learn programming first?
faq.a: for the file-reading exercise here, the useful starting skill is explaining the task and checking the source material. this guide does not ask you to write code or approve commands you do not understand.

faq.q: what should i try before giving it my inbox?
faq.a: supply a small packet of non-sensitive files and ask for a source-based outline. review missing or mistaken points before giving the bot access to a connected account.
